clue.text: Stays in charge to interrupt forecast

definitions.note: plural noun: stays are a corset, a laced garment stiffened with whalebone

indicators.note: the short piece breaks into the middle of the verb for predicting, so it sits inside that word

parts.note: to bode is to foretell or portend

explanation.surface: Someone in authority butts in on a weather forecast and stays put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' reads as a verb but is the old noun for a corset; BODE (forecast) is broken open by IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays are an old corset, and the laced, fitted upper part of a woman's dress descends from that garment.

clue.text: A pain mostly there in chest? Start to exhale

indicators.note: the shortened word goes inside the word for chest

parts.note: bosom is the chest or breast

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so the last letter of there is dropped
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone with chest pain is told to begin breathing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of 'there'; 'Start to' takes the first letter of exhale. 'A pain' fits because 'it's a pain' means it's annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something irritating or troublesome is a nuisance, informally a pain in the neck.

clue.text: Think about jail?

definitions.meaning: to consider something carefully and at length
liberate means set free, and adding the undoing prefix de- in front would mean to take freedom away, to imprison

explanation.definitionFit: To ponder over a matter is to weigh it up; whimsically, removing someone's liberty by un-freeing them amounts to locking them up.

clue.text: Couple finishing off fancy sweets

wordplay.reading: the closing pair of letters of FANCY, joined by a conjunction

parts.note: a couple here is a pair of letters, the two that close the word fancy, named one after the other with the joining word between them

explanation.surface: A pair polishes off some elaborate confections.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Couple' as a pair of letters: the two that end FANCY are C and Y, so the answer is spelt out as C, AND, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Candy is the American word for confectionery such as boiled sweets and chocolates.

clue.text: Extremely pompous and touchy sort of cow

definitions.note: to cow someone is to intimidate them, a verb

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, so take those from pompous
a sort of something is a variant of it, so the letters of touchy are rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of a pompous, irritable bovine character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' looks like the animal of the surface, but it is the verb meaning to daunt; the PS from pompous is followed by YCHOUT, a rearrangement of touchy.
explanation.definitionFit: To psych out an opponent is to unnerve and intimidate them, just as cowing someone frightens them into submission.

clue.text: A funny scooby doo episode?

parts.note: Scooby-Doo is a cartoon Great Dane with a shaggy coat, whose sidekick is even called Shaggy, so an episode of the show is literally a tale about a hairy hound; the real phrase is a long rambling joke with a pointless punchline

explanation.definitionFit: A long rambling joke with a deliberately feeble ending is a funny tale, and a cartoon about a hairy hound would be one too.

clue.text: Meeting point where explorer gets into shelter

indicators.note: the explorer's name goes inside the word for shelter

parts.note: cover is shelter or protection
James Clark Ross was a British polar explorer, giving the Ross Sea its name

explanation.surface: An explorer takes refuge at a rendezvous.
explanation.walkthrough: ROSS, the polar explorer, goes into COVER (shelter).
explanation.definitionFit: A place where two things intersect or merge, such as a road junction or a blend of genres, is where they meet.

clue.text: Outstanding work of Pindar read out

indicators.note: a poem read out is spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the poem

parts.note: Pindar was an ancient Greek lyric poet famous for his odes

explanation.surface: A recitation of a fine poem by the Greek poet Pindar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like praise for the poem, but it means unpaid, as in an outstanding debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt still unpaid is outstanding, money that remains due.

clue.text: Film-maker, rubbish one

parts.note: tat is cheap, shoddy goods, rubbish
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a director as one of the worst.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacques Tati was the French comic director of Monsieur Hulot's Holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Tati was a celebrated French director and actor, famous for his comic character Monsieur Hulot.

clue.text: Parliamentary process aimed only at heading off Tory revolts

indicators.note: the letters revolt against their order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of Tory is removed

explanation.surface: A procedure in Parliament designed solely to head off rebellions by Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' takes T from Tory, leaving ORY; 'revolts' rearranges that with AIMED ONLY AT. In the House of Commons this is a motion tabled by backbench MPs, rarely debated.
explanation.definitionFit: In the UK House of Commons, MPs table these motions to register views or gather signatures, a formal parliamentary procedure rarely given debating time.

clue.text: See parts to flog in stock left after deal

indicators.note: the little word splits the longer one into two pieces, sitting between them

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat or flog them
lo is an old word meaning look or see, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Advice on looking at which bits of the inventory to sell off after a business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests commerce, but 'deal' is a card deal and 'stock' the undealt pack; 'See' is LO, which 'parts' TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games the cards remaining in the pack after the hands are dealt form the stock, known by the French-derived name used in patience.

clue.text: Sudden discovery a short time after clumsy warning

indicators.note: the abbreviated time is placed following the other pieces, at the end

parts.note: taken as written
ham, as in ham-fisted, means clumsy
an omen is a portent or warning
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A brief moment passes after someone gives a bungled warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a short time' looks like MOMENT itself, which is a trap; 'after' puts the abbreviation T at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: A eureka-style flash of insight, when a puzzle suddenly makes sense, is exactly this kind of sudden discovery.

clue.text: One using special biology terms?

indicators.note: special here means specially rearranged, so the letters of the two words are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A scientist who talks in technical biological jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: this scientist studies life in its early stages, and pregnancy is measured in terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist who studies the development of organisms before birth uses the vocabulary of biology, and pregnancy itself is spoken of in terms.

clue.text: Good law easing supply for Scot

indicators.note: read as supple-y, in a flexible way, so the letters of law and easing are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A relaxed new law on provision of goods, intended for Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like provision, but it is the adverb from supple, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Glasgow is a Scot from Scotland's largest city.

clue.text: Us financial interests briefly spread into personal money supply

indicators.note: the shortened word goes into the word for the purse-like holder

parts.note: a wallet holds a person's cash and cards

indicators.note: briefly means the word for spread is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to strew is to spread or scatter

explanation.surface: American money is spread through someone's own funds.
explanation.walkthrough: STRE (STREW, spread, cut short by 'briefly') goes into WALLET. 'Us' stands for US, the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York street of the Stock Exchange is a byword for America's banking and investment sector.

clue.text: Was singer Romeo's spotted outside dead drunk?

indicators.note: the word for spotted goes around the letter for Romeo, enclosing it

parts.note: spotted means seen
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of dead stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone's singing was seen, while dead drunk, outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo suggests a lover singing below a balcony, apt for the answer. SEEN goes outside R, then ADED is a rearrangement of dead, signalled by 'drunk'.
explanation.definitionFit: To serenade someone is to sing to them, so having done it means having performed as a singer.

clue.text: A sensible person knocked senseless?

parts.note: someone alert and switched on who has been hit on the head is dazed and confused, no longer in touch with what is happening

explanation.definitionFit: Someone dazed after a blow is confused and out of touch, just as someone unfashionable is behind the times.

clue.text: Criminal's lost in holiday home

indicators.note: the criminal has lost the little word, so those letters are dropped from it

parts.note: a villain is a criminal; the 's reads as has
taken as written

explanation.surface: A criminal goes missing in someone's holiday home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word placing the criminal in the house, but it is the piece dropped from VILLAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a detached house, often rented abroad for a vacation.

clue.text: Satisfied about religious books and sacred music

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for satisfied goes around the books

parts.note: to have met a demand is to have satisfied it
OT is the Old Testament, a set of religious books

explanation.surface: Someone content with scripture and choral music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satisfied' is the past tense as in 'met a need'; 'about' wraps it round the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A short polyphonic choral piece, usually set to a Latin religious text, is a classic form of church music.

clue.text: Gay girl's dancing around daughter's fabulous tree

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the daughter's letter, enclosing it
dancing letters move about, so gay and girls are rearranged

parts.note: the 's is read as an s, giving girls
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A cheerful girl dances around her daughter's storybook tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' means belonging to fable, not wonderful; the tree is from Norse myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse mythology the great ash that binds the nine worlds together is a legendary tree of fable.

clue.text: What befits those in trouble, receiving variable quantity?

definitions.text: What befits those in trouble, receiving variable quantity?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters receive the variable, taking it inside them
letters in trouble are disordered, so befits and those are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
x is the standard symbol for an unknown or variable quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A question about what punishment suits wrongdoers, getting an uncertain amount.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a caning of six strokes, the classic British school punishment, befits pupils in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A beating of six strokes with a cane was the traditional schoolboy punishment, deserved by those who had misbehaved.

clue.text: Stand in line, slowly move ahead

indicators.note: ahead means the moving word comes first, in front of the letter for line

parts.note: to ease something is to move it gently and gradually

explanation.surface: Advice to queue patiently and inch forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand in line' reads as a queue, but 'Stand' alone is the definition, an artist's frame; EASE goes ahead of L.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's easel is a wooden frame on legs that holds a canvas upright, a kind of stand.

clue.text: Take a photo and lose it

definitions.meaning: to photograph something quickly and casually
to lose one's temper suddenly and shout

explanation.definitionFit: A quick photograph is a snapshot; suddenly losing one's temper is breaking under strain, both covered by one short verb.

clue.text: Muslim provided American backing

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the two short words are read from right to left together

parts.note: if means provided that
US stands for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: Someone stipulating that an American gives support.
explanation.walkthrough: IF US, read backwards as a whole, gives the answer; 'backing' looks like support.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sufi is a Muslim mystic following the ascetic, devotional branch of Islam.

clue.text: Fa support won't start more trouble

parts.note: sweet FA is British slang for nothing at all, so FA stands for nought

indicators.note: the word for support loses its opening letter

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge or arch

explanation.surface: A musical note's support refuses to begin, causing further difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fa' looks like the sol-fa note, but here it is FA as in 'sweet FA', British slang for nothing. 'won't start' takes the P off PIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who is more mischievous than another is more of a handful, so 'more trouble' works as a comparative adjective.

clue.text: Half-inch square piece of cloth

definitions.note: a verb in Cockney rhyming slang: half-inch rhymes with pinch, meaning steal

parts.note: a wipe is a cloth for cleaning

explanation.surface: Instructions for a small square of fabric measuring half an inch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-inch' looks like a measurement, but it is Cockney rhyming slang: half-inch = pinch, British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal verbs meaning to steal or pilfer something.

clue.text: Virgin can, when taken by force

indicators.note: the container word takes in the small piece, holding it inside

parts.note: to prise something open is to force it
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A suggestion about what happens when a pure young woman is overpowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb but is a container, taken inside the word for force, as in prising a lid open.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untouched and unspoiled, like virgin snow, is in perfect, original condition.

clue.text: Design an alien world

parts.note: a plan is a design or scheme
ET is the alien in the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: An instruction to draw up a world for extraterrestrials.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet is a celestial body orbiting a star, and our own is called the world.
